An extraction and novelty evaluation framework 
for technology knowledge elements of patents
Tingting Wei1,2 · Danyu Feng1 · Shiling Song1 · Cai Zhang1 
Received: 23 January 2023 / Accepted: 4 March 2024 / Published online: 10 May 2024 
© Akadémiai Kiadó, Budapest, Hungary 2024
Abstract
Technology knowledge elements play an important role in technology innovation. How-
ever, there is still challenges about their extraction and evaluation. Traditional methods 
exhibit limitations in precisely linking key technologies with functions, and they usually 
focus on measuring the overall novelty of patent documents rather than individual technol-
ogy details, leading to poor interpretability and practicality of research outcomes. In this 
work, we present a framework that extracts technology knowledge triples and evaluates the 
novelty of triples based on deep learning model. This framework first identifies key sen-
tences that reflect innovation from patent claims and then extracts technology knowledge 
elements from these sentences. A novelty index is then designed to evaluate the novelty of 
these technology knowledge elements based on the probability of their occurrence and the 
similarity to existing knowledge. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness 
of the proposed method. The extracted technology knowledge elements can use to con-
struct an innovation knowledge graph, which provides practical applications in engineering 
knowledge retrieval, design and innovation support.
Keywords  Technology knowledge elements extraction · Novelty evaluation · Technology 
innovation · Patent mining

Introduction
In the field of measuring innovation through the scientific literature, Knowledge Elements 
(KEs) represent the smallest units of knowledge (Wang et  al., 2022). KEs serve as the 
foundation for knowledge management activities and are often referred to entities. A col-
lection of KEs can represent a given technology filed (Strumsky et al., 2015). The extrac-
tion and evaluation of KEs can provide a better understanding of technology development, 
reveal new technological trends, and infer possible areas of technological development 
(Yoon et al., 2017; Zanella et al., 2021). It can also help researchers to derive and evalu-
ate new technology ideas (Hong et al., 2022), facilitate product development (Lee et al., 
2020), and identify emerging technologies (Kim et  al., 2019). By discovering potential 
technology development methods, the extraction and evaluation of KEs can help identify 
technology opportunities. Therefore, it can be considered a subtask of Technology Oppor-
tunity Analysis (TOA) proposed by Porter and Detampel (1995). Regarding the definition 
of "Method Knowledge Elements (MKEs)" as proposed by Wang et al.(2022), this paper 
delineates "Technology Knowledge Elements (TKEs)" as knowledge elements associated 
with designs, techniques, functional effects, and other technical details indicative of tech-
nological innovation. The primary focus of this paper is to extract and evaluate TKEs from 
patents, which represent the internal knowledge embedded within scientific documents.
In recent years, scholars have increasingly turned their attention towards the granular 
content within scientific documents (Zhang et al.,2023), and patent documents have been 
widely used to extract technical knowledge (Lee, 2021). Based on the results of patent 
analysis, researchers can obtain technical inspiration of designing new functions (Hong 
et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2020) or recommend key technical fields (Jin et al., 2021). How-
ever, existing patent analysis methods such as bibliometrics (Zhao et al., 2020; Stek et al., 
2021), semantic topic clustering (Ma et al., 2021; Hu et al., 2022), and keyword extraction 
from patent abstracts (Lee et al., 2020; Geum & Kim, 2020) have limitations in captur-
ing the detailed information of specific innovations, and the analysis achieved tend to be 
coarse-grained. In addition, these methods may not capture the relations between technical 
elements (Zhao et al., 2020; Altuntas et al., 2020). To summarize, existing methods for 
extracting or evaluating technology knowledge elements (TKEs) may enable the discovery 
of technological hotspots, such as promising areas or functional effects in certain technol-
ogy fields. However, the conclusions drawn from bibliometric or technology topic analysis 
are often based on subjective summarization. And researches relevant to novelty evaluation 
based on patent data typically focuse on measuring the novelty of patent documents rather 
than the novelty of specific technology details. Traditional methods exhibit limitations in 
precisely linking key technologies with functions, and they usually focus on measuring the 
overall novelty of patent documents rather than individual technology details, leading to 
poor interpretability and practicality of research outcomes.
To address the challenges mentioned, this paper proposes a framework based on deep 
learning to extract and evaluate technology knowledge elements. This framework first uti-
lizes detailed information from unstructured data in patents, such as patent claims, to iden-
tify sentences that reflect innovation and then extract technology knowledge elements from 
the sentences. These elements are represented as nodes and edges in an innovation knowl-
edge graph. A novelty index is then designed to evaluate the novelty of these triples based 
on the probability of their occurrence and the similarity to existing knowledge. Finally, a 
valid experiment is conducted by comparing the novelty annotated by three researchers 
with the novelty obtained by the proposed method, demonstrating the effectiveness of the

proposed approach. In addition, a comparative experiment is performed to further validate 
the proposed novelty evaluation method.
The contributions of this paper are as follows. First, a comprehensive framework for 
extracting knowledge related to technological innovation from patent claims is proposed. 
This framework uses the BERT model to identify sentences that reflect innovation based on 
the verbs associated with functional effects, and then employs the UIE model to perform 
key triple extraction. This process provides a data foundation for achieving fine-grained 
TOA analysis. Second, a triple novelty evaluation index based on graph neural networks 
is designed. This index enables a more objective evaluation of the novelty of combinations 
of technology knowledge elements. Third, an annotated dataset is constructed that can be 
used to validate the effectiveness of the novelty evaluation method. In summary, the pro-
posed approach aims to facilitate the identification of novel functions and corresponding 
key technologies, which can benefit technology opportunity analysis by providing a more 
objective and comprehensive evaluation of technological innovation.
The structure of this paper is as follows: the "Literature Review" section examines the 
theoretical foundations and prior researches on patent mining and novelty evaluation. The 
"Methodology" section details the framework and methods employed in this study. The 
"Illustration" section presents the results of the demonstration. The "Discussion and Con-
clusions" section delves into the implications, strengths, and limitations of the research 
presented in this paper.
Literature review
Patent mining
Patent mining refers to the process of extracting valuable information and insights from 
patent documents. It involves the systematic analysis and interpretation of patent data to 
discover trends, patterns, and knowledge related to technological advancements and com-
petitive intelligence (Abbas et al., 2014). The goal of patent mining is to gain strategic 
insights, identify emerging technologies, assess patent portfolios, and make informed deci-
sions regarding R &D or innovation strategies.
A current trend is to automatically analyze patent documents using software and algo-
rithms to extract relevant content for technological innovation (Guo et al., 2022). Some 
research analyze patents' structured bibliographic items such as International Patent Clas-
sification (IPC) codes or citation information. Cho et al. (2021) employed a Decision Tree 
(DT) based approach to forecast potential IPC co-occurrences, aiming to predict poten-
tial instances of technology convergence. Nakai et al. (2018) employed LSTM to forecast 
the trend of citation network's expand, thereby extracting the progression of technology 
development. Although these methods are objective, intuitive, and efficient, they merely 
rely on statistic information and unable to incorporate textual semantics into their analysis. 
Other research analyze patents' unstructured text such as abstracts (Ren & Zhao, 2021). 
Yoon et al. (2019) used Generative Topology Mapping (GTM) and the Local Outlier Fac-
tor (LOF) to identify vacant technology areas in the field of Information and Communica-
tions Technology (ICT) through the key word vector of patents. Lee et al.(2020) employed 
a three-layer neural network to derive Word2vec word vectors from patent data and con-
structed a product map by calculating the similarity matrix of these word vectors, offering 
insights into the current state of technological advancements. Zhang et al. (2021) combined

topic vectors obtained through Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) model with the pat-
ents' release timeline, to discover the evolution trajectory of various technologies in the 
blockchain field. The extracted technical hot-spots are regarded as the most promising tech-
nical opportunities. This type of research aims to identify technological opportunities by 
extracting semantic information from unstructured text, allowing the acquisition of more 
comprehensive, profound, and intricate insights compared to traditional statistical data. It 
facilitates fine-grained analysis of technological aspects.
Thus, this paper intends to extract semantic information (such as TKEs) from patent 
texts and facilitate in-depth patent mining. In addition, most of the current related research 
on patent analysis is based on analyzing the full text of patent abstracts, and the amount of 
data processing is relatively large. Therefore, this paper conducts a sentence-level patent 
analysis, which may simplify the data processing task. The patent claims are long texts 
containing many words and complex semantic relations. Therefore, a framework is further 
designed to extract semantic TKEs in the patent claim, with the purpose of providing inspi-
ration for developers and improving the value of the analysis.
Novelty evaluation
The definition of novelty varies across different contexts. In the field of news reports' nov-
elty evaluation research, novelty refers to a report that discusses a topic for the first time 
in a chronological sequence of news reports (Allan et al., 1998). In the process of technol-
ogy scouting and substantive patent examination, novelty generally refers to the fact that 
the content of the patent document has not been disclosed in whole or in part by any rel-
evant prior art before the priority date or filing date (Verhoeven et al., 2016). In the evalu-
ation of technological achievements, novelty refers to the fact that the research topic has 
not appeared in a specific retrieval dataset or exhibits significant differences compared to 
previous results. This concept is known as relative novelty and constitutes a primary focus 
of measurement in existing research.
Novelty carries different meanings depending on the specific scenarios and can be 
measured using various features such as contribution sentences, topic words or key 
words. Hasan et al. (2009) proposed a novelty evaluation method based on patent con-
tent, the time when the terms of patent were initially proposed was employed to repre-
sent patent's novelty. Arts et al. (2018) measured the similarity between technologies by 
calculating the Jaccard value between patent keywords, providing a method of evalu-
ating patent novelty and finding technical opportunities. Wang et al. (2019) employed 
Implicit Semantic Analysis (ISA) model to extract the relation between words in pat-
ent documents, subsequently employed outlier detection methods to identify abnormal 
patents, considering outlier patents as novel due to their divergence from the majority 
of patents. De et al. (2021) calculate the novelty of the articles by matching the text 
with a knowledge graph. Novelty is inversely proportional to the number of common 
nodes between the medical concept subgraph and the corresponding subgraph of knowl-
edge graph. A higher novelty score indicates a greater difference between the text and 
existing knowledge, indicating higher levels of innovation and uniqueness. Wang et al. 
(2022) utilized the cloud similarity equation to calculate the similarity between differ-
ent types of research contribution sentences and combined contribution sentences of 
the same type into a cloud. A low cloud similarity, denoted by a small overlapping area, 
indicates a high degree of novelty. Wang et al. (2023) proposed a framework to meas-
ure the novelty of scientific literature based on research contributions. The framework

utilizes deep learning and cloud models to identify and classify contribution sentences, 
facilitating the rapid identification of highly creative articles within a large corpus of 
papers.
In summary, the meaning of novelty varies depending on the specific context and can 
encompass aspects such as being the first report, absolute novelty from scratch, rela-
tive novelty, and differences from existing results. When evaluating novelty, factors such 
as publication date and novelty of patent content can be taken into account. Based on 
the aforementioned method of measuring differences between knowledge elements, this 
paper designs a novelty index to calculate the differences between semantic combina-
tions of TKEs.
Methodology
Research framework
This paper proposes a framework for extracting and evaluating TKEs, intending to reveal 
innovations in specific domains and analyze potential technological opportunities. There-
fore, corresponding steps are designed to achieve the above goals, as shown in Fig. 1.
After collecting patent documents, the required bibliographic item "Claims" is 
extracted. The doccano platform (Nakayama et al., 2018) is chosen to annotate sentences 
and the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model is fine-
tuned to classify the original sentences into two groups: sentences that indicate innovation 
and sentences that can not indicate innovation. Then, entities and relations in sentences 
that represent innovation are annotated, and the Unified Structure Generation for Unified 
Information Extraction (UIE) model is used to extract innovation triples. Finally, the evalu-
ation of each triple's novelty based on Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods and 
Knowledge Graph Embedding methods is employed; a visualization of the result is also 
presented, revealing the technology hotspots. Since this article is not aimed at analyzing 
the path of technological evolution, the result of visualization is only presented to indicate 
what this knowledge element extraction and evaluation method can find out.

Innovation sentences identification based on BERT
BERT is a pre-trained model that can be used for text classification tasks (Devlin et al., 
2018). In the pre-training stage, the BERT model uses the [MASK] label to cover some 
words. A two-way self-attention mechanism is designed to learn the semantic information 
of each word through predicting the missing token. And a linear classifier (in this case, a 
softmax layer) is trained for sentence classification.
This paper utilizes a fine-tuned BERT model to identify "innovation sentences" that 
indicate innovative accomplishments, making the proposed framework allow for sentence-
level analysis. And the Doccano platform is used to annotate these innovation sentences. 
The basis for the annotation is the work of Korobkin et al. (2019), which discovered high-
frequency verbs that refer to functional effects. Since innovation in technology involves 
substantial improvements or evolution at the technical level based on existing technologies, 
leading to the generation of new products, processes, and methods (Edwards-Schachter, 
2018), the novelty of functional effect could be considered as a representation of the degree 
of innovation. Therefore, sentences identified based on verbs that indicate functional effect 
should be able to reflect technological innovation in a way.
The process of identifying innovation sentences could be viewed as a binary sentence 
classification task, achieved by using a fine-tuned BERT model and linear classifier. After 
extracting patent claims and segmenting the sentences, they will be sorted into two groups: 
"innovation sentences" and "non-innovation sentences". Only innovation sentences will be 
included in subsequent analysis and used as a data source to extract key triples.
Key triples extraction based on UIE
Innovation sentences identified by the BERT-based method serve as a data source for key 
triple extraction. The types of entities and relations are designed based on the high-fre-
quency verbs discovered through Subject-Action-Object analysis, and the Doccano plat-
form is used to annotate the entities and relations. The annotated sentences are then split 
into three datasets (train set, dev set, and test set) to fine-tune the UIE model. Finally, 
the fine-tuned UIE model is used to extract triples from unannotated sentences. These 
extracted nodes and relations reflect the functional effects of patents and can be considered 
key triples in the analysis of innovation. Thus, the extraction of TKEs can be viewed as the 
joint extraction of key triples from innovation sentences.
UIE model is applied to implement the joint extraction of innovation entities and rela-
tions (Lu et al., 2022). UIE uses SEL (Structured Extraction Language) to describe the 
hierarchical relation in the training text and uses a Structural Schema Instructor (SSI) to 
control which information is extracted. SSI is a Schema-based Prompt engineering that 
guides the identification and association of specific information. By utilizing SSI, the gen-
eration of SEL can be effectively guided and semantic information can be shared among 
different labels and tasks.
The original UIE can uniformly generate different information extraction structures. 
When performing the relation extraction task, the [spot] label represents the entity, and the 
[asso] label represents the relation. The model first identifies different segments according 
to the labels in front of the sentence, namely "Spotting", and then determines the rela-
tion between these segments, namely "Associating", as is shown in Fig. 2. By using these 
labels, UIE is promoted to predict new SEL structures from sentences without any label.

Specifically, assuming there is an input text sequence x and SSI s, UIE first calculates 
the hidden representation H = {s1, … , si, x1, … , xi} for each token. Then use the encoder 
to generate the linear SEL sequence of the target record y = {y1, … , yi} , and the decoder 
will decode the hidden representation and the previously generated SEL sequence to pre-
dict the token in the following SEL sequence.
The UIE algorithm used in this paper comes from the open-source code of Baidu Pad-
dle Studio (PaddleNLP Contributors, 2021). On the basis of the original UIE paper's idea, 
Paddle-UIE applies the attention mechanism mentioned above and uses the Transformer-
based ERNIE 3.0 model (Sun et al., 2021) to perform information extraction tasks. The dif-
ference between the paddle's UIE model and the original paper is that as a discriminative 
model based on a fixed prompt, Paddle-UIE performs better in zero-shot tasks and few-shot 
tasks with an advantage in speed. Instead of estimating the distribution of the joint prob-
ability like generative models, the discriminative model uses conditional distribution for 
classification (Ng & Jordan, 2001). This paper choose paddle's UIE to extract triples for 
the advantage metioned above.
Novelty evaluation based on HGT and TransH
The traditional novelty evaluation methods mainly focus on the whole patent level, less 
considering the innovation of fine-grained technical knowledge. In addition, due to the 
possible semantic overlap among triples of fine-grained technology knowledge triples 
extracted from the patent claims, the semantic complexity makes it difficult for the tradi-
tional node influence-based methods to effectively measure the novelty of the triples. To 
solve this problem, this paper performs novelty evaluation on the extracted triples from the 
perspective of semantic similarity, following the approach proposed by Luo et al. (2022).
Our proposed method defines novelty as the distinctions and uniqueness of a knowledge 
element in comparison to existing knowledge. When a combination of knowledge elements 
has a low probability of occurrence in a network, it implies a weak connection with other 
known combinations of knowledge elements, indicating a greater distance in the vector 
space (Hain et al., 2022). Thus, low occurrence probability can be interpreted as higher 
novelty of the triple. Furthermore, the semantic similarity of the text reveals the distinc-
tions in semantic roles and functions within the contextual semantic environment of words, 
which plays an important role in reflecting novelty (Luo et al., 2022). Scholars (Arts et al., 
2018; Wang et al., 2019) have used semantic similarity to assess novelty and obtained simi-
lar results that align with real-world observations. In this paper, a novelty index is devel-
oped incorporating both the combination probability of knowledge elements and semantic

similarity, reflecting the differences between specific triples and existing triples in the 
domain and thus capturing the novelty of the triples.
To identify triples that can reflect technological innovation from the extracted key tri-
ples, a novelty index is designed for the evaluation of novelty. Evaluating novelty implies 
comparing with existing knowledge. This paper considers a triple to be novel if it has a low 
probability of occurrence. The novelty of triples is evaluated by measuring the degree of 
novelty of the methods or technologies represented by them. Therefore, the lower the prob-
ability of a triple appearing in the knowledge graph, the higher its novelty is considered 
to be. This paper combines knowledge graph embedding models and entropy weighting 
methods to design a novelty evaluation method that incorporates both link probability and 
semantic similarity of technology knowledge elements. Figure 3 illustrates this approach.
The Heterogeneous Graph Transformer (HGT) (Hu et al., 2020) is a graph neural net-
work designed to model large-scale heterogeneous graphs within the web domain. By pre-
serving type-specific parameters, it enables specialized representations of different node 
and edge types, facilitating the modeling of the heterogeneous structure. Notably, HGT 
incorporates a novel attention mechanism that automatically learns important "meta-paths" 
without manual design, making it highly effective in handling heterogeneous graph data. 
This attention mechanism has shown promising results in various real-world applications. 
In this paper, HGT is employed to obtain representation vectors of nodes and edges in the 
knowledge graph, which are subsequently used in further computations.

Experiments and results
Data collection and preprocessing
Agricultural robots are automated devices used in agricultural production. They can sig-
nificantly improve agricultural production efficiency, reduce labor costs, save energy and 
reduce environmental pollution in agricultural production (Zhao et al., 2020). Agricultural 
robots may become a vital force in planting and farming. However, current research on 
agricultural robots is still in the laboratory stage, and it is still difficult to apply fully auto-
matic and precise control on robots in practical applications (Jin et al., 2021).
Based on the fact that agricultural robots are capable of automating many agrarian 
tasks such as planting, watering, fertilizing, harvesting, and packaging agricultural prod-
ucts. This paper designs a query set using keywords like "mechanical arm", "agricultural 
robot", "harvest robot" and so on, as shown in Table 1. Then the query set is used to col-
lect patents of USPTO from the "Zhihuiya" website. In total, 1343 patents of the search 
result are related to agricultural robots and are selected for subsequent analysis.
The patent claim is a detailed document that describes the technical details of an inven-
tion which could be considered as technology knowledge elements. As the original text 
data is unstructured, preprocessing steps, such as segmentation of relevant paragraphs, are 
carried out to prepare the data for a deep learning model. A total of 40,113 sentences are 
obtained for further analysis.
Innovation sentences identification
Patent claims contain valuable information about new technologies, making them an 
important source for technology analysis and innovation research. Based on the work of 
Korobkin et al. (2019), who extracted descriptions of physical effects from patent claims in 
the USPTO database, predicates such as "change", "increase", "decrease", "depend", "gen-
erate", "act", and "cause" are considered suitable for describing the technical benefits of 
patents. These verbs reflect significant functional improvements from the old technology to 
the current patent and can be considered as evidence of technology innovation. Therefore, 
sentences in patent claims that contain these words are considered "innovation sentences", 
meaning that they contain technology knowledge elements and can reveal innovation. Then 
the BERT model is utilized to extract such innovation sentences.

A total of 40,113 sentences are collected, out of which 29,291 sentences are annotated. 
Among these annotated sentences, there are 3004 innovation sentences. To construct the

Logistic Regression, TextCNN, and TextRNN, are compared through experimental anal-
ysis. As shown in Table 3, the results on the self-constructed dataset demonstrated that 
BERT produced the best performance among the models. In the end, a total of 4150 inno-
vation sentences are obtained.

python 3.8.16, Tensorflow 2.6.2 and CUDA 11.2 to perform innovation sentence recogni-
tion, a binary classification task. After multiple rounds of iterative adjustment, the model 
achieved a F1 value of 0.97 on the test set.
Then the fine-tuned model is utilized to classify the remaining 10,822 sentences into 
the appropriate category. The unannotated samples are input into the model to complete 
the task of identifying innovative sentences. Based on the identification results, every pat-
ent contains innovation sentences, indicating that the self-constructed dataset has achieved 
comprehensive coverage of relevant patents. In total, 4209 innovation sentences were 
obtained, with an average of 3.13 innovation sentences per document.

Novelty evaluation
The key triples extracted through UIE consist of TKEs that represent functions, designs, 
technologies, etc. However, not all key triples can reflect technological innovation, as some 
triples are common in patent documents and cannot distinguish one patent from another 
in the same field. Therefore, the proposed novelty evaluation method is applied to identify 
novel triples that reflect both functional effects and the novelty of technological innovation. 
Figure 5 shows the number of each relation type among all novel triples.

novel evaluation method is compared with existing evaluation method. A validation dataset 
is constructed manually to assist in testing the accuracy of the proposed method, and the 
comparative experiment and an annotation consistency test are utilized to ensure the fea-
sibility of manual evaluation. The valid data set consisting of 310 triples is annotated by

Application of innovation knowledge graph
The innovative knowledge graph can serve as an infrastructure for broad uses and applica-
tions in engineering knowledge retrieval, design and innovation support. For example, the 
innovation knowledge graph can be used to search the relevant knowledge elements around 
them according to semantic relationships for learning and enhancing design ideas. Such 
semantic relationships can also contribute to the query for solutions to specific engineering 
design problems or functions. In addition, clustering of nodes within the knowledge graph 
can yield functional technical solutions.
Figure 6 illustrates the application procedure of the innovation knowledge graph and 
its role in TOA analysis. With the constructed knowledge graph, users can retrieve infor-
mation from the KG (Knowledge Graph) database and identify Problem-Solution triples, 
such as (H)Technology-< Solve>-(T)Problem or (H)Technology-<Achieve>-(T)Function, 
facilitating the formulation of solutions for specific functions or technical problems. Addi-
tionally, users can utillize community detection algorithms to identify significant nodes or 
clusters, which may represent current technology hotspots. This approach can also reveal 
functional technical solutions by identifying shared approaches to similar problems within 
each cluster. Figure 7 shows examples of the triples that reflect Problem-Solution. Figure 8 
shows an example of the relatively important cluster. The meanings of each triples are 
shown in Table 12.

Discussion and conclusions
Our approach focuses on extracting and evaluating the technology knowledge elements 
with functionally-meaningful semantic associations from patent claims. By contrast, 
the previous study only mined patent titles and abstracts, and the type of knowledge is 
rather monotonous. Our work also contributes to a more comprehensive understanding 
of technological landscapes. The generated triples of technology knowledge elements 
could input into Neo4j to construct an innovation knowledge graph, which can serve as 
a valuable tool for guiding future innovations and identifying technology hotspots and 
trends for researchers in the field.
In present work we utilize advanced deep learning techniques and knowledge graph 
embedding models to identify and evaluate technological innovation in a more effective 
and objective manner. However, there are great potentials to derive even better-perform-
ing method in future research via improving the quality of training data, fine tuning the 
procedures, and exploring alternative techniques, as well as expanding the application 
of innovation knowledge graph.
Firstly, due to the segmented structure of patent claims, resulting in semantic seg-
mentation in content, our study extracts sentences individually from each paragraph, 
inadvertently ignores a lot of semantics. A potential enhancement could involve seg-
menting patent claims based on semantic criteria before sentence extraction, which 
would contribute to obtaining sentences that are more semantically comprehensive. Sec-
ondly, the types of nodes and relations of technology knowledge triples could be bet-
ter designed based on more comprehensive pre-work, such as conducting more detailed 
SAO analysis or using expert-summarized guide examples. In addition, our approach 
exclusively evaluate the novelty of technology knowledge triplets through semantic sim-
ilarity. Nonetheless, given the intricacies of semantics and the heterogeneity present in 
patent claim formulations, it may not achieve precise and comprehensive evaluation of 
the novelty of technology knowledge. In the future, exploring the incorporation of some 
network structural factors on top of semantic similarity could enhance the robustness 
of this method and broaden its applicability to diverse patent contexts. The third is to 
continually enhance and evaluate the quality of innovation knowledge graph by incre-
mentally updating more technology knowledge elements and involving more human 
expert evaluators. This will facilitate the exploration of broader applications for our 
constructed knowledge graph.
